correctness.rationale: A closed analytic trace-class perturbation family has a simple isolated lambda2 eigenvalue at the disk. Direct basis matrix differentiation and the infinite-dimensional second-order eigenvalue formula give the claimed coefficients, including exact cancellation of m=1. For all R>0, monotonicity of t_k/S_k follows by positive-term comparison (R/(k+1)) S_{k-1}=sum_{j=3}^k[j/(k+1)]t_j<S_k. The endpoints q2 and lim q_m yield all regimes. Finite-section numerical checks corroborate the formula but are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The exact second-eigenvalue Hessian addresses a motivated open optimization hierarchy beyond Gaussian Faber-Krahn. Two sharp changes in the sign structure of all angular modes distinguish local disk geometry and inform the radial-annulus/nonradial symmetry-breaking problem. Rigidity of the translation mode and the full infinite harmonic spectrum provide structural information beyond straightforward isolated numerical examples.
